narrative.summary: The Council of Europe adopted the first binding international treaty on AI, the Framework Convention on AI and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (opened for signature in 2024), backed by the HUDERIA risk and impact assessment methodology and model. Its Committee of Ministers has adopted recommendations on algorithmic systems (2020), profiling (2021) and equality and AI (2026), and declarations on manipulative algorithms and AI in social welfare. Specialised bodies have issued guidance on AI and data protection, facial recognition, AI in judicial systems and generative AI in courts, and AI in journalism, and the Parliamentary Assembly adopted a package of AI resolutions in 2020.

The Council of Europe AI page lists 21 signatories (Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Canada, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Liechtenstein, Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, Ukraine, United Kingdom, United States, Uruguay and the European Union), with the European Union as the only Party. instruments.summary: First legally binding international treaty on AI, requiring Parties to ensure that activities across the AI lifecycle are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, with obligations on transparency, oversight, accountability, risk and impact management, and remedies. It covers public authorities and private actors acting on their behalf, and Parties choose how to address other private-sector activities.

instruments.current_status: Opened for signature in Strasbourg on 28 January 1981; in force 1 October 1985. Article 8 gives data subjects rights over automated processing, and the amending Protocol (CETS 223, 'Convention 108+') adds the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions.
instruments.summary: The first binding international treaty on data protection: Parties must protect individuals' personal data in automated processing, with principles on lawful and fair processing, data quality, special categories, data security and data-subject rights, and rules on transborder data flows. It underpins rules on automated decision-making used in AI governance, strengthened by the 2018 amending protocol (Convention 108+).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding data-protection treaty governing automated processing of personal data, the legal basis for rights over automated decisions in Parties' AI governance.

instruments.official_title: Protocol amending the Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data (CETS No. 223)
instruments.english_title: Protocol amending the Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data (CETS No. 223)
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of Europe (Committee of Ministers)
instruments.publisher_name: Council of Europe (Committee of Ministers)
instruments.summary: Protocol modernising Convention 108 ('Convention 108+'). Among other updates, the amended Convention's Article 9(1)(a) gives individuals the right not to be subject to a decision significantly affecting them based solely on automated processing of data without having their views taken into consideration, and Article 9(1)(c) gives the right to obtain, on request, knowledge of the reasoning underlying data processing whose results are applied to them.
instruments.current_status: Done at Strasbourg on 10 October 2018. Under Article 37 it enters into force once all Parties to Convention 108 have consented to be bound or, failing that, five years after opening for signature for the consenting States provided there are at least 38 Parties.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date from the closing formula 'Done at Strasbourg, this 10th day of October 2018' in the treaty text on rm.coe.int (read 2026-10-21).
